exposure — What is really owned once every fund is looked through to what it holds, as of a date (default today). Views: classes; sectors (by class and sector); sizes (large, mid, small caps); countries (with region); currencies (the fiat currency, metal or coin a value moves with); credit (debt by rating bucket, IG or HY); maturities (debt and cash by time to maturity); coupons (fixed, floating, inflation_linked, zero); cycles (equity by cyclical, sensitive, defensive); situs (the country whose law each holding sits under; no fund looked through, so not exposure); securities (each security, direct and through funds); issuers (stock, bonds and deposits together, largest first, with the running share); funds (each fund held, what describes it and how old that is); coverage (what the figures rest on and what nothing describes). Every view sums to net worth: share_pct is of it; class_share_pct is within the row's dimension (its class on sectors and sizes; every row but (none) on credit, maturities, coupons, cycles), so those sum to 100. Read quality and coverage before trusting a figure. period with from/to: the view at the end of every month, quarter or year, in one call. Example: {view: "countries", as_of: "2025-12-31"}; quarter by quarter: {view: "countries", period: "quarterly", from: "2025", to: "2025", filter: ["country = US"]}.

Parameters (all optional):
  view         classes | sectors | sizes | countries | currencies | credit | maturities | coupons | cycles | situs | securities | issuers | funds | coverage. Which breakdown (default classes).
  as_of        As-of date. Default today.
  country      risk | domicile. countries and securities: the country a security counts in, risk (default) or domicile.
  benchmark    the benchmark's weight of each row and the row's share less it; not on situs, funds or coverage, and no period. One of Global 60/40, Global 80/20, S&P 500, US total bond market, World (ACWI), or a name from the config's benchmarks block.
  period       monthly | quarterly | annual. classes, sectors, sizes, countries, currencies, credit, maturities, coupons, cycles, situs and coverage: a series at the end of each period of from/to (default: the last twelve months).
  from         With period: the series' start (YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, today, yesterday, last month, last year).
  to           With period: the series' end, same forms. Default today.
  currency     Output currency, e.g. USD or CHF. Default: the configured one.
  filter       Conditions, all of which hold: ["value > 1000", "date >= 2025-07", "category not in Rent, Groceries"].
  search       Keep rows with this text in any cell.
  columns      "default", "all", names, or "+add,-remove"; describe(topic=<tool>) lists them.
  sort         Column to sort by; "-" for descending. "-value": the main money column, largest first whatever the sign.
  max_chars    Most characters the result may take (default 16000); the page ends at a row boundary and the last line says how to get the rest.
  limit        Most rows to return (default: as many as fit).
  offset       Rows to skip (default 0).
  format       table | csv | json. Result format (default table).

Columns (* = shown by default; columns=all shows every one):
  classes: asset_class*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, quality*
  sectors: asset_class*, sector*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct, via_funds_pct, class_share_pct*, quality*
  sizes: asset_class*, size*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct, via_funds_pct, class_share_pct*, quality*
  countries: country*, country_name*, region*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, quality*
  currencies: currency*, kind*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, quality*
  credit: bucket*, grade*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, class_share_pct*, quality*
  maturities: bucket*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, class_share_pct*, quality*
  coupons: coupon_kind*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, class_share_pct*, quality*
  cycles: cycle*, value_USD*, share_pct*, direct_pct*, via_funds_pct*, class_share_pct*, quality*
  situs: situs*, country_name*, region*, value_USD*, share_pct*, funds_pct*, quality*
  securities: security*, name*, ticker, asset_class*, sector*, country*, currency*, market_cap, size, value_USD*, direct_value_USD*, via_funds_value_USD*, funds, share_pct*, quality*
  issuers: issuer*, lei, value_USD*, share_pct*, cumulative_share_pct*, equity_pct*, debt_pct*, cash_pct*, securities, quality*
  funds: fund*, name*, value_USD*, share_pct*, via*, proxy*, leverage, provider*, basis, composition_date*, gap_days*, lines*, weight_sum_pct*, domicile, situs, situs_basis, replication, lending, hedged_currency, declaration_date*, declared*, quality*
  coverage: section*, reason*, items*, value_USD*, share_pct*, detail*, silver_source_id*, instrument*

Filters each view takes (a filter the view lacks moves the call to the first finer view that has it):
  classes: none
  sectors: none
  sizes: none
  countries: none
  currencies: none
  credit: none
  maturities: none
  coupons: none
  cycles: none
  situs: none
  securities: none
  issuers: none
  funds: none
  coverage: none

Every view sums to net worth, as holdings view=global gives it: what a fund's composition does not explain is a remainder row, and a holding nothing describes is unknown, never dropped. A fund's composition is the one nearest the as-of day (the funds view says which, and how old); quality flags such as proxy, aged or partial carry the share of the row they touch (describe topic=quality). view=situs reads every holding whole, at its legal situs: it looks through no fund, and its quality says what each situs rests on; coverage's situs section lists the holdings whose situs is unknown. The view sums are in the output currency; the shares need none.
Example: {view: "sectors", as_of: "2025-12-31", currency: "CHF"}.
